text:
sam_w: Pushing chart v2.4.1 to staging, deploy-bot kicked off a canary but it auto-paused. Seeing node-drain eviction spikes during the EU maintenance window. Not sure if the chart affinity tweak caused it to concentrate pods on a smaller set of nodes. Anyone oncall? :eyes:

deploy-bot: Automated pause: canary (chart=payments-service:2.4.1) paused due to 6 pod restarts and 30% eviction errors within 3m. Reason: node.eviction.window_overlap with scheduled maintenance. See /deploy/logs/4481234567

anna_dev: ack. timeline? is this the pre-scheduled EU drain at 02:00 UTC?

sam_w: yes, the cluster autoscaler/maintenance drain was scheduled at 02:00. Canary started ~01:50 and got into trouble when the node drain started re-scheduling pods. Chart change was an affinity -> preferredDuringScheduling entry to shove db-proxies to same AZ. didn't think it would reduce spread that much.

chris_sre: quick check: PDB for payments has minAvailable: 2, replicas=5 so it should tolerate drains, but affinity can co-locate and cause more than 3 pods to move at once. Can you paste the values override?

sam_w: pasted below (only the relevant snippet):
```yaml
replicaCount: 5
podDisruptionBudget:
  enabled: true
  minAvailable: 2
affinity:
  podAntiAffinity:
    preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
      - weight: 100
        podAffinityTerm:
          topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
          labelSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app: payments-service
```

maya_pm: we need a fast rollback plan. options: 1) pin to 2.4.0 and re-run, 2) hotpatch values (remove affinity) and resume canary, 3) postpone maintenance window. Ops preference?

chris_sre: postpone maintenance isn't ideal (infra already warned). Pin rollback will revert unrelated bugfixes in 2.4.1. I prefer a values hotfix: set affinity -> remove the antiAffinity block or lower weight, and increase PDB minAvailable=3 to be safer. Then resume canary manually.

anna_dev: +1 for values override. Quick patch command I ran in a dev cluster earlier:
```bash
helm upgrade payments-service redwood/payments --version 2.4.1 --set affinity.podAntiAffinity.preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution=null --reuse-values --namespace staging
# or use a small JSON patch with kubectl if you want granular change
kubectl -n staging patch pdb payments-pdb --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/minAvailable","value":3}]'
```

sam_w: doing the values override now. Will push a staging override config and then trigger deploy-bot resume.

deploy-bot: Heads-up: manual resume requires a comment with the justification and `--manual-resume` flag. See /docs/deploys/resume-policy

sam_w: resume request posted. comment: "hotfix values: remove antiAffinity + increase PDB to 3 to avoid co-eviction during scheduled node drains. Verified smoke tests pass locally."

chris_sre: before resume, can we also add a temporary nodeSelector to spread pods across zones? e.g., `topology.kubernetes.io/zone: any` won't work but we can relax affinity weight to 50 instead of 100. Safer than full removal.

anna_dev: updated plan: set weight=50 and PDB.minAvailable=3. I'll prepare the values-override file and attach to the resume.

maya_pm: timeline: if we apply now and resume within 10m, infra will finish drains and we should be fine. Ops confirmed they can delay the last 5m of the drain if we signal quick resume.

sam_w: override applied, smoke tests OK. deploy-bot resume call in 30s.

deploy-bot: Manual resume approved by: anna_dev, chris_sre. Resuming canary for payments-service:2.4.1. Observing for 15m health window.

sam_w: :thumbsup: watching logs; no new evictions so far. Pod distribution looks better.

chris_sre: watch for 95th latency on the service, affinity change may affect cache locality. If we see >200ms tail increase, we'll abort and roll back to 2.4.0.

sam_w: noted. adding a regression check to the smoke job to fail the canary if tail latency rises.

maya_pm: once canary clears, we need a short release note blurb: "2.4.1 fixed auth header bug; temporary rollout adjusted affinity and PDB to mitigate co-eviction during node drain. No end-user impact observed." I'll draft.

sam_w: canary passed at 15m. No regressions. marking as promoted to staging -> prod queue.

maya_pm: thanks team. Follow-up action: open a ticket to revisit the affinity change for a longer-term solution (spread constraints + rack-awareness) so we don't rely on PDB hacks. I'll create that. :spiral_notepad:
